subject: Geopolitics
title: Afghanistan: Cycle of Intervention
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Afghanistan: Cycle of Intervention.

hook.text: The Soviet Union invaded in 1979. The US invaded in 2001. Both left defeated. The Taliban returned both times.

buildup.text: Afghanistan's rugged terrain and tribal structure make central control nearly impossible.

discovery.text: Two decades of US nation-building collapsed in days.

twist.text: Trillions spent on roads, schools, and armies vanished because local legitimacy was never built.

climax.text: Afghanistan shows that foreign powers cannot create states from outside. Legitimacy must grow from within.

punchline.text: Build a state from outside and it falls when you leave.

quiz.question: Why did US-built institutions collapse so quickly in Afghanistan?
options: The US withdrew military support too slowly
Local legitimacy and loyalty were never established
Afghanistan lacked the natural resources to sustain them
